perspective:
Mason’s available information:

- He is an accountant at a small community center, and Martha Moua is a personal care aide there; they are work colleagues with mainly professional interactions.
- He reviewed financial reports and observed discrepancies: healthcare expenses seemed unusually high compared with usual spending.
- He initially suspected Martha might be mismanaging funds, which made him suspicious and anxious.
- He raised the discrepancy with Martha. He heard her say there may have been a misentry and that she would review and correct errors.
- After reviewing the report with Martha, he concluded the discrepancies were a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. He felt relieved but embarrassed about his earlier suspicion.
- He apologized to Martha. He heard her accept the apology, say errors happen, understand that he was being thorough, and suggest double-checking entries next time.
- He now believes Martha is competent and that the financial management system is inadequate. He feels frustrated with the system but empathetic toward Martha.
- He proposed creating a new, more robust financial system and asked for Martha’s input. He heard her agree and offer to help identify gaps.
- He drafted a proposal for the new financial system. He hopes it will benefit operations but is uncertain whether management will approve and implement it.
- He discussed the draft with Martha. He heard her call it solid, encourage presenting it confidently, and agree to help gather supporting data.
- He prepared a detailed presentation and asked Martha to help gather data to strengthen their case; she agreed.
- He presented the proposal to management. He feels satisfied with his effort but physically and mentally exhausted. He believes he has done everything he can and that the decision is now up to management.
- He told Martha the presentation went well and it is up to management. He heard her praise his work, suggest taking time off, and offer help while he is away.
- He plans to take a few days off to recharge and reflect, hoping for good news upon return.
- He does not yet know management’s decision about the proposal.
